name: atomization-migration-doctrine
claim: Wholesale atomization of conjunctive descriptive nodes proceeds as a regenerable parallel-graph migration rather than per-node supersession: decomposition judgment lives in a reviewed spec (plans/atomize/spec.json), generation is deterministic (mix cb.migrate.atomize, emitting beliefs/cb-atomic), and identity is preserved - an aggregate-disposed node keeps its id and claim, retypes to aggregation, and grounds in newly minted single-sentence atom attestations. This extends the cb:b051 vocabulary-migration precedent (in-place, identity-preserving structural correction) from labels to grounding; the swap into beliefs/cb is a separate, reviewed replacement commit.

evidence.detail: Operator stipulation: the graph's immutability is aspirational rather than practical at current adoption, correctness outranks strict ceremony, and the wholesale migration is authorized as a parallel DAG with id-and-claim-preserving retypes. Descriptive lane executed this session: 31 aggregations over 115 atoms (cb:b700-b814), 2 inference trims, 24 keeps; output verifies 20/20 schema checks.
